_comment: What an mds analysis should be cited with: the statistics it computes and the R packages it
computes them in. Merged with PoolSeqFlow, Nextflow and R by the frame, and written into every
published folder as CITATIONS.md and references.bib.
This file is the one to edit; it compiles to citations.json beside it with
dev/scripts/bib2citations.py, and 00_static fails when the two disagree.
A 'note' says what the entry is cited FOR. A method is not a tool, so an entry for one names
no r_package and no version is asked of anything: what is credited is the estimator.
THE DISTANCE ITSELF IS CREDITED IN analysis/references.bib, NOT HERE. nei_distance() is
library code that any module placing or clustering pools calls, so its citation belongs to the
layer rather than to this module - the same rule that puts n_eff there. A BibTeX key may be
defined once across the whole manual, and this module's own citation is the ordination it
ggplot2 and jsonlite are credited in analysis/references.bib for the same reason.
GENERATED from references.bib beside this file. Do not edit it: dev/scripts/bib2citations.py overwrites it, and 00_static fails when the two differ.

gower1966.name: Classical multidimensional scaling
gower1966.title: Some Distance Properties of Latent Root and Vector Methods Used in Multivariate Analysis
gower1966.note: The ordination this module draws: a matrix of squared distances double centered into a Gram matrix, whose leading eigenvectors are the coordinates. It is what R's own cmdscale cites and implements, and the source of the negative eigenvalues this module publishes rather than hides - they are what a distance matrix that no flat space holds exactly produces.
